newsitem.title: GERMANY: IG Metall - early retirement scheme a "priority".
newsitem.headline: IG Metall - early retirement scheme a "priority".

text.p: IG Metall, Germany's largest trade union, said on Wednesday that agreement over a plan that would allow early retirement in the metal and engineering sector was an "absolute priority" in talks with employers over a reform of the sector's collective bargaining rules.
"This is an absolute priority," IG Metall chairman Klaus Zwickel told journalists before going into talks with the Gesamtmetall employers federation.
"Young workers must be given a possibility of employment in the sector and old workers must be allowed to move into retirement under acceptable circumstances," he added.
Gesamtmetall president Werner Stumpfe had earlier stressed the need to make existing wage agreements more flexible. He said the rigidness of existing worker contracts disadvantaged German firms.

Stumpfe said that he welcomed a suggestion mooted by Zwickel that future wage contracts, rather than being valid for the millions of workers across the metal and engineering sector, should be tailored to meet the needs of specific industry branches.
He said however that he did not expect overall agreement on the reforms before the end of the year.

Union officials are hoping that talks will return to a model they have already proposed that would allow workers effectively to retire five years early while retaining their full pension entitlements.

Under the proposed model, 55-year-old workers would receive 85 percent of their full salary for the last 10 years of their working life. They would then work full-time for five years before being released at the age of 60.
